title: Fleet heatmap observations and weekly action log
content:
Fleet heatmap observations and weekly action log (2026-03-29 to 2026-03-31)

Purpose:
- Capture observed utilization patterns from the fleet heatmap for last 72h, highlight region-level divergence, and record follow-ups for capacity/planning.
- Short, actionable items for infra + SRE to reduce cold-starts and avoid cross-region spill during anticipated Apr weekend traffic.

Attendees (sync 2026-03-31 10:00 PT):
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marcus Chen (infra lead)
- Lina Gómez (SRE)
- Noah Reed (capacity planning)
- Sofia Martinez (release eng)
- Observers: two rotating on-call engineers

Executive summary:
- US-west utilization spiked to 85% sustained during 2026-03-30 02:00–05:00 PT due to a combination of batch-embedding jobs and two customer tail-bursts. Heatmap shows contiguous "hot corridor" across us-west-1a/b/c.
- eu-central shows stable 48% with several short-lived hotspots aligned with nightly eval runs (INF-2345).
- APAC (ap-northeast) utilization low (23%) but cold-start rate higher than baseline: 9% of requests triggered model load vs historical 3.5% — indicates cache churn or eviction policy issues.
- Prewarm pool fill for p4d-type nodes at 00:00 UTC dropped to 60% on 03-30 due to autoscaler scaling steps and a mis-specified min-ready flag in the policy (PR to follow).

Key metrics (72h window, rolling):
- avg GPU util (cluster-wide): 54%
- us-west peak util: 85% (03-30 02:15–04:45 PT)
- cold-start rate: 6.1% (cluster), ap-northeast: 9%
- prewarm hit-rate: 78% overall, p4d pool: 60% during peak window
- tail token latency (95p): +18% in us-west during peak (observable in tracing)

Root-cause hypotheses / notes:
1) Batch embedding jobs from internal analytics were not throttled; they started a large sweep at 01:50 PT (linked ticket GPU-6789). These jobs were configured to prefer zone-local capacity which amplified the us-west corridor.
2) Autoscaler cooldown logic allowed a downscale step between bursts; combined with min-ready misconfig leads to under-filled prewarm pools.
3) APAC higher cold-starts appear correlated with eviction of prefix cache entries when sequence-length distribution spiked for a small set of customers — investigate cache retention policy per-region.

Decisions and short-term mitigations (agreed in meeting):
- Immediate throttling: Noah to post a rate-limit override for internal analytics batch jobs for next 48h (INTERNAL-TICKET: INF-PT-archive) — target: reduce us-west sustained util by 15% within 24h. Due: 2026-04-01 16:00 PT.
- Prewarm policy fix: Marcus to land a quick patch to set p4d prewarm min-ready to 80% and extend autoscaler cooldown from 2m->6m for high-variance pools. Rollout on canary cluster tonight (03-31). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4312.
- APAC cache retention tuning: Lina to run an experiment with 1.5x KV-cache retention for ap-northeast for 72h, compare cold-start and tail latency. Tagging change: exp/cache-apac-2026-04-01.
- Cross-region spill policy: temporarily cap on-demand cross-region routing for non-enterprise traffic at 10% to prevent overloading us-west. Release eng (Sofia) to coordinate config change in routing layer.

Medium-term actions (this sprint):
- Capacity rebalancing proposal: Noah to draft a region hedging plan that shifts 12% of reserved p4d capacity nominally from eu-central to ap-northeast to reduce cold-starts and improve latency for APAC. Deliverable: capacity request doc + cost delta. Due: 2026-04-07.
- Heatmap-driven autoscaling research: Aisha to scope an RFC for heatmap-integrated autoscaler that considers cross-zone skew and sticky prewarm affinity. RFC due: 2026-04-14.
- Observability: add a per-model prefix-eviction metric to heatmap pipeline; Lina to open metric request (METRIC-req-114).

Incidents / anomalies logged this week:
- 2026-03-30 03:10 PT: transient latency burst in us-west, escalated to P2. Mitigated by manual throttling of one large customer job. Postmortem draft in Confluence: Fleet-incident-2026-03-30.
- 2026-03-29 22:45 PT: autoscaler misfire leading to rapid scaling down in one zone; rollback executed and rollback playbook updated (see linked PR).

Open questions / blockers:
- Can we safely increase global prewarm budget by 6% without breaking cost targets for Q2? Finance sign-off required. (Assign: Noah -> CFO sync).
- Need confirmation from Model Onboarding team if large nightly evals can be moved to off-peak windows or staggered. (Assign: Aisha to sync with Model Onboarding).

Action items (owner - due):
- Noah Reed - post batch-job throttles + update internal runbook - 2026-04-01 16:00 PT
- Marcus Chen - land prewarm min-ready + increase cooldown on canary + monitor - 2026-04-01 23:59 PT
- Lina Gómez - run ap-northeast cache retention experiment, collect metrics - 2026-04-04
- Sofia Martinez - apply routing cap config and validate spill metrics - 2026-04-01 20:00 PT
- Aisha Patel - draft RFC for heatmap-integrated autoscaler - 2026-04-14
- Noah Reed - capacity rebalancing proposal doc - 2026-04-07

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Quick win: increase the prewarm readiness health-check timeout from 10s->30s for p4d images to avoid false-negative readiness and reduce prewarm churn. Marcus will include this in the PR.
- Suggested small experiment next week: run a mirrored traffic test from eu-central to ap-northeast for one hour to validate routing and cold-start behaviour. Need budget approval.

Appendix: useful links and dashboards
- Fleet heatmap (ops dashboard): https://dash.redwood.ai/fleet/heatmap/rolling-72h
- Prewarm pool dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/fleet/prewarm
- Incident postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Fleet-incident-2026-03-30
- Related tickets: INF-2345, GPU-6789, METRIC-req-114

TL;DR: us-west corridor overheating due to unthrottled batch jobs + autoscaler cooldown gap; short-term throttles and prewarm policy fix should reduce tail latency. APAC needs cache retention tuning and modest reserved capacity rebalancing to reduce cold-starts.
